benchmark_kind: single-host A/B correctness and cost measurement
protocol: MP-SPDZ Semi, three local parties, preprocessing included
scope_warning: One tiny synthetic fixture (10 real entities, 3 owners, 3 relations) on a single host. Do not extrapolate latency or communication to MetaQA, WebQSP, WAN, or production deployments. This fixture is deliberately the worst case for the paged layout; see headline_finding.
headline_finding: On this fixture the relation-paged backend is SLOWER than the packed scan: 13.9897 s vs 12.1341 s and 3524.11 MB vs 2798.19 MB global. This is the expected and correct outcome, not a regression. The paged layout narrows a bucket from max-source-degree to max-(source,relation)-degree; on a fixture where those are 2 and 1 there is nothing to narrow, so the added directory level is pure overhead. Its advantage is asymptotic and appears only when the source-wide fanout bound would otherwise have to be large, which is exactly the uncapped high-degree case the packed scan cannot represent at all.

relation_paged_backend.layout: directory 33 rows x 3 owners, page pool 16 rows x 2 slots per owner, pages_per_key=1

observed_ratio_paged_over_scan.note: Ratios above 1.0 mean the paged backend costs more on this fixture.

correctness.comparison: Exact JSON equality of all four reconstructed ranked rows per query, against two independently implemented cleartext oracles.
correctness.note: Agreement with the packed-scan oracle also confirms the two layouts are semantically equivalent on inputs both can represent.

what_this_does_not_show: Any lossless high-degree result: this fixture fits both layouts, so it does not exercise overflow pages.
Any WAN or multi-host result; all three parties ran on one machine, which does not instantiate the non-collusion assumption.
Any malicious-security property; the runtime is MP-SPDZ Semi, which is passive-only.
